title: My Pineapple Tallow Balm Experiment: Or, How I Stopped Fighting My Skin
body:
Okay. So I was trying to write this last night but my neighbor’s TV was so loud. Some reality show. Anyway. I’m just gonna type this out because I keep telling people about this weird little jar of stuff and then having to explain it five times. It’s easier to just… put it somewhere.

I got this whipped tallow balm. The pineapple one. Beef tallow skincare. Sounds insane, right? Like, putting beef fat on your face. I thought it was a joke. A weird crunchy mom thing. But my skin was just… done. With everything else.

## The Whole Reason I Even Looked For This Stuff

It was this specific cream. The La Roche-Posay Lipikar Balm AP+. Everyone online screams about it. For dry, sensitive skin. It’s like twenty-five bucks. I bought it because my hands last winter. They looked like a topographic map of Mars. Cracks. Red lines. It hurt to make a fist. So I got this fancy French pharmacy balm. Slathered it on.

It felt like I’d dipped my hands in plastic wrap.

Seriously. It just sat there. This greasy, shiny film. I’d touch my phone and it’d be a smeary mess for an hour. I tried to type and my fingers would just slide off the keys. And underneath that gross layer? My skin was still thirsty. Still tight. Still cracking. It was like putting a raincoat on a dying plant. Looks covered, but nothing’s getting in. I used almost the whole bottle hoping it would “start working.” It didn’t. My sink had this permanent oily ring. I was so mad. Wasted money, wasted time, still had sandpaper hands.

That’s when I got desperate. And annoyed. And started googling things like “what did people use before lotion.” Which is how you end up on forums talking about rendered animal fat.

## Why Beef Tallow for Skin? (It Sounds Gross, I Know)

Look, I get it. The ick factor is high. I stared at the Etsy listing for this Pineapple Tallow Balm for like, three days. Whipped beef tallow. From grass-fed cows. Made in some small kitchen in France. The pictures looked nice. Creamy. But my brain kept going: *This is for cooking. Not your face.*

But then I read one thing that made a stupid amount of sense. Human skin oil—sebum—is mostly triglycerides, right? Squalene, wax esters. Beef tallow? Almost identical fatty acid profile. It’s like… your skin recognizes it. It’s not some alien, lab-made silicone or mineral oil. It’s a fat that our biology actually knows what to do with. It absorbs. It doesn’t just clog the door; it gets invited in.

So I bought it. As a joke, almost. A “well, this will be a funny story” purchase. I got it from this shop called [Etsy Shop Name - you should insert the actual shop name here if you know it, otherwise keep it generic]. The jar was smaller than I thought. Fits in the palm of your hand.

## What This Pineapple Tallow Balm Actually Does

Opening it was an experience. It doesn’t smell like beef. At all. Which was my first fear. It smells like… a pineapple Lifesaver candy. But not in a cheap, fake way. More like if you walked past a smoothie stand on a hot day. Sweet. Bright. Cheerful. It’s a vacation smell. It made me happy immediately, which is not how I usually feel about skincare.

The texture is weird. In a good way. It’s whipped, so it’s super airy and light in the jar. You scoop a little—you need way less than you think—and it melts the second it hits your skin warmth. It goes from this waxy balm to almost nothing. No dragging. No pulling.

Here’s the big difference versus that La Roche-Posay plastic-wrap balm: it disappears. Like, actually sinks in. I put it on my horrible cracked knuckles before bed. No greasy film. I could pick up my water glass immediately. And in the morning? The cracks were just… less angry. Not gone, but softer. The skin around them wasn’t tight. After three days, the cracks started to close. Not with a weird scab, but the skin just decided to knit itself back together.

I got brave and tried it on my face. I have this dry, flaky patch on my cheek that comes every spring. Windburn, maybe. Or just my skin being dramatic. My usual CeraVe moisturizer would calm it for an hour, then it’d be back. I put a tiny dab of the tallow balm on it. Felt rich. Kind of luxurious, honestly. Woke up, and the patch was just… normal skin. No flakes. No redness. Just gone.

It doesn’t feel like you’re wearing anything. That’s the magic. It’s not a layer *on* your skin. It becomes part of your skin. You just feel like you have good skin. Not moisturized skin. Just… healthy skin.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Weirdness

I’ve been using it for maybe a month now? My nighttime routine is just: wash face, pat dry, tiny scoop of the pineapple balm. That’s it. My skin is quieter. It’s not “glowing” in that Instagram way. It just looks like itself. Balanced. Not oily by noon, not dry by 3 PM. My hands are finally, finally human hands again. No cracks. I can wash dishes without wincing afterward.

The best part is the simplicity. I’m not layering three serums and a moisturizer and an oil. I’m using one thing. One ingredient, basically, plus some pineapple essential oil for smell. That’s the whole “natural vs commercial skincare” thing, I guess. The commercial stuff has a list of 40 ingredients, half of which are stabilizers and emulsifiers and preservatives to make that cream sit on a shelf for three years. This tallow balm? It’s food. It goes bad eventually. Because it’s real.

I’m not a purist. I still use my fancy sunscreen. But for moisture? This little jar has replaced a whole shelf of products that didn’t work. I’m on my second jar now. I got one for my mom, who has even more sensitive skin than me, and she texted me last week saying “what is this wizardry.”

So yeah. It just works. I don’t have a more complex review than that. It solved a problem I was spending a lot of money and energy on.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Weirdly, yes. Because it’s so similar to our own skin oils, it absorbs deeply instead of sitting on top. It’s like giving your skin something it actually knows how to use for repair. My face has been happier since I started using it.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was worried about this too. But no—for me, it didn’t. Because it absorbs, it’s not just blocking pores up. It’s non-comedogenic. My skin feels clear. If you’re super acne-prone, maybe patch test, but it’s been fine for my combo skin.

**What does the pineapple tallow balm smell like?**
Exactly like it sounds. Sweet, fruity pineapple. Not artificial candy, but like a really ripe, fresh pineapple. It’s a happy smell. Makes putting on moisturizer feel like a little treat.

Anyway. If you’re frustrated with lotions that feel gross or don’t work, this might be worth a shot. It’s definitely the best natural moisturizer I’ve stumbled upon. I got mine from that Etsy shop, and I’ll probably order another one soon before I run out. My skin’s happy, I’m happy. That’s the whole tallow balm review, I guess.
